title: Project 2: number guessing game

understand.concept: A number guessing game generates or selects a target, accepts repeated guesses, validates input and reports whether each guess is low, high or correct. It should define attempt limits and avoid relying on predictable random sequences for security-sensitive uses.
understand.whyItMatters: The project combines loops, decisions, input validation and state tracking in a manageable interactive program.

explain.narrative:
A number guessing game generates or selects a target, accepts repeated guesses, validates input and reports whether each guess is low, high or correct. It should define attempt limits and avoid relying on predictable random sequences for security-sensitive uses.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The loop reads guesses until the input conversion fails or the correct value is entered. A complete version should distinguish invalid input from end-of-file and may use a random target.

practise.independentTask: Add a validated attempt limit and a replay option. Explain how the target is selected and how random seeding works.
hints: Use a deterministic target in tests so expected behaviour is repeatable.
Do not use rand for cryptographic or security-sensitive randomness.
Handle end-of-file and invalid input intentionally.
